radiology_report:
Ziekenhuis Gelderse Vallei (Ede)
Department of Radiology
Date: 07 Feb 2025
Exam: mpMRI prostate

Clinical indication: Re-evaluation of prostate cancer. PSA 7.8 ng/mL. Prior biopsy Gleason 3+4.

FINDINGS:
Prostate volume: 23.44 mL. T2-weighted imaging demonstrates a focal lesion in the peripheral zone at the base, right side, measuring approximately 18 x 15 mm. The lesion is markedly hypointense on T2WI. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows restricted diffusion with high signal on b=1400 and corresponding low ADC values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences demonstrate early, intense enhancement of the lesion. No extracapsular extension is identified. Seminal vesicles appear uninvolved. No suspicious lymphadenopathy or osseous metastases.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right base of the prostate.
PSA density 0.333 ng/mL/mL.
Clinical T stage cT2.
csPCa predicted probability 0.8538012.

previous_notes.author: Dr. M. Jansen (GP)
previous_notes.text: 18 Feb 2023 - Dr. M. Jansen (GP): Patient presented with elevated PSA of 2.6 ng/mL. Transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsy was performed. Pathology returned Gleason 3+4, ISUP grade group 2, with cribriform pattern and intraductal carcinoma present. Perineural invasion noted at the right base. Discussed findings with patient; opted for active monitoring. Referred to urology for specialist follow-up.

previous_notes.author: Dr. M. Jansen (GP)
previous_notes.text: 12 Jun 2024 - Dr. M. Jansen (GP): Follow-up visit for prostate cancer surveillance. PSA measured at 5.4 ng/mL, showing a rise from previous values. Patient reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms. No new neurological or musculoskeletal complaints. Arranged repeat PSA in three months and scheduled urology re-evaluation.

pathology_report:
Biopsy specimen, 18 Feb 2023:
Histological examination of the prostate tissue reveals acinar adenocarcinoma. The Gleason score is 3+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 2. High-risk patterns are present, specifically cribriform pattern and intraductal carcinoma (IDC-P). Perineural invasion is identified. The tumour is located at the base, right.

Trajectory summary: The current biopsy findings confirm the previously established diagnosis of ISUP grade group 2 prostate cancer with high-risk features, maintaining the same histological grade group since the initial sampling.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 5.
